messages:
Maria: Heads-up — reproducible memory growth on Dedicated for tenant 'alpha' when serving long-context chat (>=80k tokens). Hosted runs same model at similar QPS show stable KV size. Suspect per-tenant pinning + eviction window config drift.

Kevin: Can you share profiler stack and memstats? Which kernel path used? Any fallback logs?

Maria: Quick paste from the pprof snapshot and memstats — large retained slabs in kv_pageframe alloc, eviction count low. Excerpt:
```text
kv_pages_active: 1.9GB
kv_pages_evicted: 120
kv_page_fragments: 42
alloc_backtrace: runtime::kv_allocate
```

Ajay: Looks like the batcher occasionally emits spikes (~512 concurrent seqs) which triggers kernel fallback to the slow path and bigger temporary allocations. Also the Dedicated runtime config has kv_pinning: per-tenant and eviction_threshold: 10%, while Hosted is using adaptive/global pinning and 2%. That combo could explain why Dedicated retains more pages.

Liz: Quick config diff I pulled from prod manifests — not exhaustive but highlights the defaults we accidentally diverged on:
```json
// dedicated config
{
  "kv_pinning": "per-tenant",
  "eviction_threshold_pct": "10",
  "kv_retention_ms": "600000"
}

// hosted config
{
  "kv_pinning": "global",
  "eviction_threshold_pct": "2",
  "kv_retention_ms": "120000"
}
```

Maria: I flipped the Dedicated test cluster to the hosted eviction_threshold (2%) and saw mem growth stop in a 4h soak. But that increases cross-tenant churn under high sustained QPS — could impact tail latency for noisy tenants.

Kevin: There's also a networking/fragmentation angle. Private on-prem boxes with MTU=1500 show higher page fragmentation vs Dedicated cloud nodes with jumbo frames (MTU=9000). Transporting KV pages across hosts (RDMA/verbs/rpc) changes alignment and recomposition costs which increases transient allocations.

Ajay: Repro plan I propose:
1) Launch 3-node Dedicated with kv_pinning=global and eviction_threshold=2%
2) Run tenant-hotspot soak for 12h (alpha workload) with periodic pprof snapshots every 30m
3) Repeat identical workload on Private box with MTU=1500
4) Collect metrics: kv_pages_total, kv_pages_reused, kv_pages_evicted, kv_page_fragments, allocator_retained_bytes

I'll script the workload — basic curl storm to simulate concurrent short-chat sessions:
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do \n  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.redwood/api/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"gptx-8k","prompt":"<80k tokens of history>","stream":false}' &\n  sleep 0.01\n done
```

Maria: Thanks — can you also hit /metrics every 5m and dump the runtime logs with log level=debug for the kv allocator? That will let us correlate eviction spikes with kernel fallbacks.

runtime-bot: Alert: kv_cache_eviction_rate spike on alpha-tenant at 1864123001 — rate changed 0.02 -> 0.0003 (automated anomaly detector).

Liz: If global pinning mitigates growth we still need guardrails: per-tenant memory quotas + a fast-path eviction circuit breaker to avoid noisy neighbor impact. Filed GH issue #498 to track follow-ups.

Maria: @Ajay I'll run the first repro tonight and post the pprof tarball tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
